title: Finitely presented etale-space fibres, descent data and cartesian realizations
statement: Fix the universes of [def-weil-size-convention] and an ambient scheme $S$ [def-pc-scheme]. Regard a scheme $T\to S$ as its representable algebraic space, using [def-trf-algebraic-space] and [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space]. Define $\mathcal F(T)$ as the full subcategory of algebraic spaces over $T$ whose structural map is chartwise etale [def-sfb-space-chartwise-etale-morphism], locally of finite presentation on etale charts [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties] and [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], quasi-compact on affine scheme tests [def-sfb-space-quasi-compact-presheaf-map], and has quasi-compact relative diagonal. Use the sheaf fibre products of [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. For $q:X\to T$, define its data category to have objects $A\in\mathcal F(X)$ with a natural transport descent datum [def-pd-descent-datum], equivalently an isomorphism of the two pullbacks with diagonal identity and triple cocycle; arrows are maps over $X$ commuting with transport. A realization consists of $B\in\mathcal F(T)$ and a map $A\to B$ whose square over $q$ is cartesian and which is invariant under transport. Describe full faithfulness of the canonical comparison by its Hom equalizer: for $B,C\in\mathcal F(T)$ and a cartesian square $P=B\times_T X$, every map $v:P\to C$ over $T$ such that $vs=vt$ whenever $ps=pt$ descends to a unique $T$-map $B\to C$. Universal descent means this Hom condition after every quasi-separated scheme base change, where quasi-separated has the convention of [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]; universal effective descent means universal descent together with a realization for every datum after every such base change. For a cartesian square $P\to X$, $V\to T$, define a cartesian map from a datum $E$ over $P/V$ to $D$ over $X/T$ to consist of a map of underlying spaces cartesian over $P\to X$ and commuting with their transports. This specifies the canonical pullback datum up to its unique compatible isomorphism, retaining actual comparison maps.
